findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
findings.citation_text:
2-201.11(E) Responsibility of Permit Holder, Person In Charge, and Conditional Employees. Responsibility of food employees and conditional employees to report. The person-in-charge did not have signed copies of the reporting agreement present for the available staff. The binder present in the bar had copies of Bassett, food handler, and CFPM. But no employee health or reporting agreement information was available. During the inspection, the employee health reporting agreement paperwork was provided as was the diagnosis and symptom paperwork. PIC was informed that it was his job to make appropriate number of copies and have staff sign the agreements. 

 (E) A FOOD EMPLOYEE or CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEE shall report to the PERSON IN CHARGE the information as specified under (A) of this section.

findings.title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events.
findings.citation_text:
2-501.11 Clean-up of Vomiting and Diarrheal Events. There was not an available policy for removal of vomit and diarrhea during the inspection. Policy paperwork was provided during the inspection by CK. Corrected on-site. 

A FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall have written procedures for EMPLOYEES to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. The procedures shall address the specific actions EMPLOYEES must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of EMPLOYEES, consumers, FOOD, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter.

findings.title: Food obtained from approved source.
findings.citation_text:
3-201.11(A) Compliance with Food Law. The facility is operating as a Class I facility. The kitchen is observed cooling and reheating a number of foods (inclusive of chicken, red sauce, cheese sauce, and chili). Cooling practices were discussed and seem appropriate. See that cooling methods are educated to additional staff supporting this behavior. Facility is operating as a Class II entity and is not currently allowed to cool and reheat but a simple upgrade of their permit classification will allow the behavior to change. The kitchen will be upgraded to a Class I kitchen and cooling and reheating may continue. 


 (A) FOOD shall be obtained from sources that comply with LAW.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.citation_text:
3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. The walk-in cooler is old and has portion of the ceiling where condensation leads to dripping. A containers of sauce that had a whole placed in the plastic wrap for cooling is observed to have water condensation accumulating on the surface. The water appears to be accumulating to one side of the plastic, but the viscous nature of the water means that possible cross-contamination cannot be ruled-out. During the inspection the water -laden contained food was discarded. 
Also, a container of single-service crackers is observed stored beneath the bug light on the counter by the dry storage. The crackers were pulled forward and away from the bug light. See that nothing is stored beneath the light. 

(A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. Observed the interior and the exterior of the triple sink to be soiled with accumulated soil and food debris. Also, the interior of the dish machine is noted to have accumulated food debris along the sides of the walls and within the external sump of the side of the dish machine. The dish machine operator was arriving around 130 and PIC stated that facility would be cleaned around that time. 

(A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures.
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16(A)(1) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. Operator initially stated that the reheating temperature was 135F and then eventually stated that reheat temperature is 165F. Stem thermometers are available as are alcohol wipes. The operator was observed to be hot holding foods at 129 to 134F. Operator eventually increased the temperature of the steam table and then covered the foods. Stem thermometer should be used to monitor the reheating of foods in double boiler to insure 165F benchmark is met. 

(A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained: (1) At 57°C (135°F) or above, except that roasts cooked to a temperature and for a time specified in 3-401.11(B) or reheated as specified in 3-403.11(E) may be held at a temperature of 54°C (130°F) or above.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.citation_text:
3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. There are two deli meats observed in the cookline preparation cooler that are beyond the seven day mark. One is hame from 9/10 and the other is a turkey product from a date in August. It is likely that the August date was an improperly scraped and washed container, however, both foods were discarded. See that dates are correctly marked, food is monitored to be discarded at appropriate time, and cleaning is conducted effectively. 

 (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.citation_text:
4-202.16 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. There is observed cardboard being used to hold single-service lids in the bar. Cardboard is not an easily cleanable material suitable for washing. Replace the cardboard with a material that is easily washable. Also, the upright freezer holding Butch’s pizzas is observed with an accumulation of frost. See that the unit is defrosted to allow for proper washing of the surface. 


NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be free of unnecessary ledges, projections, and crevices, and designed and constructed to allow easy cleaning and to facilitate maintenance.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.citation_text:
4-303.11(B) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. Upon initial entrance to the facility, there was no sani-bucket available. During the inspection a bucket was created for the kitchen. The bar had a bucket available and that bucket was recreated after the first waive of diners left and counters were wiped. The bucket was created using the wall-mounted chemical. Solution was tested at 200ppm Quat.  

(B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.citation_text:

The refrigerator within the kitchen is also noted as having some soil related to splash. 


 (B) The non-FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations.

findings.title: Toilet facilities: properly constructed, supplied, and cleaned.
findings.citation_text:
6-202.14 Toilet Rooms, Enclosed. The employee bathroom does not have a self-closer. Provide a self-closer for this bathroom. 

Except where a toilet room is located outside a food establishment and does not open directly into the food establishment such as a toilet room that is provided by the management of a shopping mall, a toilet room located on the PREMISES shall be completely enclosed and provided with a tight-fitting and self-closing door.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.

(A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.

findings.citation_text: 6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; or (C) A heated-air hand drying device; or (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures. [Pf]

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: Inspector observed chicken being stored above milk in the walk in cooler. CORRECTED- the PIC moved the chicken below the milk. Milk is considered a “ready to eat” (RTE) food item, which should always be stored above animal proteins to avoid cross contamination. Items should be stored according to cooking temperatures; with the items requiring the highest cooking temperature stored below items that require lower cooking temperatures to- no cooking.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.

The prep cooler is not holding TCS items at or below 41F, so PIC and inspector discussed using time as a control for food safety (TAC), or cold holding items on ice, until the prep cooler is serviced (see violation #33). Inspector discussed proper methods for cold holding on ice, as well as the 4 hour limit for TAC.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the prep cooler to have an ambient temperature of 47F. PIC was notified, and a work order was placed to have the unit serviced. Ensure cold holding units are able to hold food items at or below 41F.
findings.citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. [Pf]

findings.title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
findings.comment: FIRST REPEAT: Multiple coolers throughout the facility were observed without ambient thermometers. CORRECTED- PIC moved extra thermometers into units lacking ambient thermometers. When placed correctly, ambient thermometers measure the temperature in the warmest part of the cooling unit. This helps the facility identify early on when cold holding units are out of temperature. Ensure all coolers (freezers do not require ambient thermometers as long as food is observed to be frozen solid) contain ambient thermometers, placed towards the front of the unit.
findings.citation_text: 4-204.112(A) Temperature Measuring Devices. (A) In a mechanically refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, the sensor of a TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure the air temperature or a simulated product temperature in the warmest part of a mechanically refrigerated unit and in the coolest part of a hot FOOD storage unit. [C]

findings.title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
findings.comment: Inspector observed multiple single service storage containers being stored on the floor in the dry storage area in the banquet room. PIC stated that shelving has been ordered to keep single service items off of the floor. Ensure food contact surfaces are stored at least 6 inches above the floor.
findings.citation_text: 4-903.11(A) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (A) Except as specified in (D) of this section, cleaned EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor. [C]

findings.comment:

2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. [C]

4-204.112: (A) In refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure air temperature. [C]

findings.comment:

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.12 Kitchen manager was observed using a wiping cloth to wipe their hands after previous discussion of proper use. Improper handwashing technique was later observed when the manual faucet was shut off without a barrier, and the handle to the paper towel dispenser was touched after handwashing process was completed. Proper handwashing was discussed. Ensure proper technique is used every time hands are washed. Always use disposable paper towels for wiping hands and not wiping cloths/common towels.
Food employees shall properly wash their hands with the following procedure: (1) rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) apply soap; (3) rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds; (4) thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying. To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.citation_text:
3-304.11 1. Plate used for storage of ice scoop on top of the ice machine was soiled with discolored splash and grimy buildup. After cleaning and sanitizing the plate was stained and had stuck on buildup. Plate was discarded by manager.

2. Soda gun holder at banquet area bar was soiled with crusty buildup and possibly dried out mold. Holder was removed to be cleaned and sanitized. 

3. Mold accumulation was observed on the metal baffle in the bin of the ice machine and along the top above the baffle. Mold was also observed inside the bin on the ceiling behind the baffle. Condensation was dripping off of areas where mold was present. Cleaning and general maintenance of ice machine were discussed. Ice machine will be cleaned and sanitized, and follow-up will be conducted to check the machine on 12/9/22.

Food shall only contact surfaces of equipment and utensils that are cleaned and sanitized as specified under Parts 4-6 and 4-7 of the 2017 FDA Food Code; single-service/single-use articles, or linens such as cloth napkins, as specified under § 3-304.13 that are laundered as specified under Part 4-8 of this Code.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:

Chemical dispensed properly after priming occurred. Concentration was observed at 100ppm. Technicians also came out for service call and verified the dish machine is functioning properly. 
A chemical sanitizer shall be used in accordance with EPA-registered label use instructions. Maintain dish machine final rinse concentration as stated on the label instructions. Use test strips to verify concentration.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
4-302.14 Quat test kits were not available for checking sanitizer solutions. Test strips were provided by technician that came out for dish machine service. Maintain both chlorine and quat test kits. Chlorine strips are needed for the dish machine and any bleach solutions (100-200ppm) used for wiping down surfaces. Quat strips are needed for sanitizer tabs at the bar and product now being used in the kitchen.
 A test kit that accurately measures the concentration of sanitizing solutions in mg/L shall be provided. Obtain and use quat test strips with sanitizer used on food contact surfaces in the kitchen.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text:
6-501.11 & 6-501.12 1. Floor drain in walk-in cooler was missing a cover. Some general buildup was observed on the inner lip of the drain. Clean the drain and provide a proper cover.

2. Floor tiles under fryer wheels were soiled with grease buildup and showing signs of wear. Tiles were cracked and need to be repaired or replaced. Provide repairs so the floor under fryers is smooth and easily cleanable.
 
Physical facilities shall be maintained in good repair and cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.citation_text:
2-102.12 Kitchen manager did not have proof of manager certification. Bartender had a food manager certification but was not the person in charge of the kitchen at the time of inspection. The person in charge of food prep/service in the kitchen needs to have a manager certification as well. Kitchen manager noted they took a course online but were unable to get their certificate printed. Ensure a copy of kitchen manager’s certification is maintained at the facility.  
Person in charge at the time of inspection shall be a certified food protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an accredited program.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.citation_text:
2-103.11 (O) Employee health documents and signed reporting agreements could not be found during the inspection. Revised versions of employee health documents were provided and discussed. All bar and kitchen staff working at the time of inspection reviewed and signed reporting agreements. Bar manager will have all other employees review and sign off on reporting agreements as they arrive for shifts. Ensure all staff are educated on the employee health policy upon hiring, and maintain signed copies of reporting agreements for staff. 
The person in charge shall ensure that food employees are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with law, to the person in charge, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through food, as specified under ¶ 2-201.11(A).

findings.title: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use
findings.citation_text:
2-401.11 Employee appeared to be eating during food prep. Employee stated they were eating an onion because they needed to taste it. The employee was actively chewing while wrapping food at the counter. If staff feel the need to taste test a food item, then care should be taken to not be doing so while actively working with food. Step away while tasting whatever is being eaten, properly wash hands, and then return to finish prep/wrapping of foods. 
Employees shall eat only in designated areas where the contamination of exposed food; clean equipment, utensils, and linens; unwrapped single service and single use articles; or other items needing protection cannot result.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.14 Employee was preparing to put on a pair of gloves for prep without first washing their hands. Prior to putting on gloves the employee was observed working over in the dish area and then handled their wallet to show inspector proof of food handler certification. Employee was advised on handwashing prior to glove use and washed hands before putting on gloves to continue with prep. 
Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles, before putting on gloves, and after engaging in activities that contaminate the hands.

findings.title: Food obtained from approved source
findings.citation_text:
3-201.11 Cheese sauce leftover from the previous evening was observed. Kitchen manager noted leftovers are not typically cooled and kept for use, but they happened to keep a small unused portion with the intent to reheat for use today. Cooling and reheating requires a Class I (high risk) certification, and the facility is currently Class II (medium risk). Cheese sauce was discarded. No other leftover cooled food items were observed at the time of inspection. (See general comments for additional information)
Food shall be obtained from sources that comply with law.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.citation_text:
3-304.11 Banquet bar soda gun and holder were observed soaking in a solution that was somewhat murky and had a chunk of debris floating in it that appeared to be mold. Soda gun and holder were cleaned during the inspection. Cleaning and general storage of soda gun were discussed. 
-Mold accumulation was observed on the metal baffle in the bin of the ice machine and along the top above the baffle. Kitchen manager cleaned and sanitized all surfaces during the inspection. A layer of ice was removed once process was complete. Cleaning and general maintenance of ice machine were discussed.
Food shall only contact surfaces of equipment and utensils that are cleaned and sanitized as specified under Parts 4-6 and 4-7 of the 2017 FDA Food Code; single-service/single-use articles, or linens such as cloth napkins, as specified under § 3-304.13 that are laundered as specified under Part 4-8 of this Code.

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used
findings.citation_text:
3-501.13 Three pans of fish were thawing in the basins of the 3 part sink. Pans in the first and third basin had standing water while fish in the middle compartment was under cold running water but not fully submerged (fish was stacked above water line in the pan). Options for thawing were discussed with emphasis on planning ahead and utilizing the walk-in cooler to thaw in advance. Two pans of fish were placed in the walk-in cooler while the remaining portion remained under cold running water. If cold running water will be used, then all the fish in the process of thawing must be completely submerged during the process. 
TCS food must be thawed: (A) Under refrigeration at 41°F/below; (B) Completely submerged under running water at a water temperature of 70°F/below, with sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose particles in an overflow, and for a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of ready-to-eat food to rise above 41°F; (C) As part of a cooking process; or (D) Using any procedure if a portion of frozen ready-to-eat food is thawed and prepared for immediate service in response to an individual consumer's order.

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.comment:
4-204-112 Thermometers were not present in the fridge and freezers used for storage in the banquet room. Provide thermometers for all refrigeration and freezer units used for storage of TCS foods. 
Cold or hot holding equipment used for time/temperature  control for safety (TCS) food shall be designed to include and shall be equipped with at least one permanently affixed temperature measuring device that is located to allow easy viewing of the device's temperature display.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.citation_text:
4-303.11 Sanitizer solution was not available for use in the kitchen and prep was underway. Bleach solution at 200ppm was prepared for use. Ensure sanitizer solution is prepared and available for use prior to beginning food prep.
Sanitizer shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

findings.title: Toilet facilities: properly constructed, supplied, & cleaned
findings.citation_text:
6-202.14  Men's room door was not shutting properly. Repair the men’s room door so it shuts properly. 
All toilet rooms located within a food establishment must be enclosed with a tight-fitting and self-closing door.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625  Sec. 3.06 Expired food handler certifications were observed. Three of the four observed were for employees that no longer work at the facility. The fourth was said to have a current food handler certification that needs to be printed. The bar manager had an expired CFM and noted they completed a food handler course but still need to provide a copy of the new certification. Ensure copies of non-expired certifications are maintained for all bar and kitchen staff on-site. 
All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.12 Food employee washed hands without proper technique. The manual faucet was shut off prior to retrieving paper towels to dry hands. Proper handwashing technique was discussed, and food employee was observed washing hands properly for the remainder of the inspection. 
Food employees shall properly wash their hands with the following procedure: (1) rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) apply soap; (3) rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds; (4) thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying. 
To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink.
findings.citation_text:
2-301.14 Food employee returned to the kitchen after placing a roll cart in the walkin cooler and did not wash hands prior to putting on gloves. Handwashing between tasks and prior to glove use were discussed. Employee was observed washing hands between tasks/as needed for the remainder of inspection.
Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles. Hands must also be washed upon entering the work area and after engaging in activities that contaminate the hands.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114 Final rinse concentration at dish machine was observed at 0ppm chlorine. Chemical bucket was full and contained new product/appeared to be recently replaced. The line was primed to attempt correcting the issue, but the sanitizer was not suctioning through the line. Detergent and rinse aid were dispensing properly. A call for service was made, and a technician arrived to fix the dish machine during the inspection. Technician replaced tubing for all the chemicals at the dish machine. All chemicals were dispensing and the dish machine was functioning properly upon conclusion of inspection. Final rinse was observed at 100ppm chlorine once the machine was repaired. 
A chemical sanitizer shall be used in accordance with EPA-registered label use instructions. Maintain dish machine final rinse concentration as stated on the label instructions (no lower than 100ppm and no higher than 200ppm). Use test strips to verify concentration of bleach solutions.
findings.citation_text:
4-602.11 Metal baffle in the ice machine had mold buildup along the side and bottom edges. All other surfaces were observed to be clean. The metal baffle was cleaned and sanitized during the inspection. Cleaning frequency was discussed. 
Equipment with enclosed components, such as ice machines, shall be cleaned at a frequency specified by the manufacturer, or absent manufacturer specifications, at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
6-501.111 Approximately a half dozen fruit flies were observed under the ice bin at the bar. Moisture and debris accumulation under the ice bin were promoting their presence. Fly management strategies were discussed, including frequent cleaning and use of fly strips in appropriate locations
The premises shall be maintained free of pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence by eliminating harborage conditions.
findings.citation_text:
6-501.112 A dead mouse and debris accumulation were observed on a glue trap under dry storage shelving. Frequent monitoring and replacement of glue traps were discussed.
Dead or trapped birds, insects, rodents, and other pests shall be removed from control devices and the premises at a frequency that prevents their accumulation, decomposition, or the attraction of pests.

findings.title: Sewage and waste water properly disposed
findings.citation_text:
5-402.13 Bucket of discolored waste water with a strong odor was observed in the banquet room keg cooler. The waste water was emptied during inspection. Manager observed a slow drip occurring at the condenser in the cooler, which was likely the source of the liquid accumulation. Ensure the bucket is emptied daily and kept clean.
All sewage and waste water must be routed to an approved sewage disposal system.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text:
6-501.12 Floor under dry storage shelving had some debris accumulation and an old glue trap containing a dead mouse. Clean the floor under the dry storage shelving.
--Moisture and debris accumulation was observed on the floor under the bar ice bin and also on the attached plumbing. Clean in this area daily/as needed to eliminate a potential harborage location for fruit flies (see #38).
Physical facilities shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean

findings.title: Sanitizing concentration
findings.citation_text:
750.830 - Sanitizer concentration at the dish machine was observed at 0ppm chlorine. Employee noted the concentration was close to 200ppm when he checked it first thing this morning. However, the chemical tubing was knocked out of the bucket during cleaning later in the day and resulted in air bubbles inhibiting proper suction of chemical through the line. After sanitizer line was primed and machine ran through multiple cycles the sanitizer concentration was observed at 100pm chlorine.

All chemical sanitizers in a dish machine must meet the requirements of 21 CFR 178.1010 to ensure all items are properly sanitized.  Rinse water shall not less than 75F. Provide proper sanitizer concentration.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
750.800b - The following food contact surfaces were soiled:
A) can opener blade (debris buildup);  and
B) inside ice machine - metal baffle (mold along side and bottom edge).
Can opener was cleaned and sanitized during the inspection. General cleaning and maintenance of the ice machine were discussed with Kitchen Manager.

Clean and sanitize food contact surfaces between uses/as needed to prevent cross contamination and eliminate buildup of debris. In-use items, such as can openers, utensils, cutting boards, etc., need to be properly cleaned and sanitized up to every 4hrs after continuous use.

findings.title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.citation_text:
750.860 - Portable radio was observed sitting on top of the clean utensil caddy in the dish area. Bottom of the radio was touching a few of the utensil handles. Radio was moved to the top of the fridge during the inspection. Manager was advised the radio may sit at the far end of the drain board if it is possible to position it between the caddy and the fridge, if the radio can be maintained clean, and if the radio can be stored in a manner that won't pose a potential risk of cross contamination.

Cleaned and sanitized utensils an equipment shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in a clean, dry location in a way that protects them from contamination by splash, dust and other means.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.citation_text:
750.1220 - Floor in kitchen dry storage area had buildup of dust, general debris, and what appeared to be some food debris under shelving (far right side of the room). Some old mouse droppings were also observed under wire shelving on the right side of the room. Clean the floor as needed to eliminate buildup and watch for potential pest activity.

Floors shall be maintained clean.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
(R) 750.151 - A) An open gallon of milk in the second kitchen fridge did not have a date mark and was less than 1/4 full. Cook stated it was open the Friday prior. Milk in question would not be used for food service; milk was labeled for personal use and kept by an employee.
B) Portions of swiss cheese and American cheese were date marked 11/10. Swiss cheese is exempt from date marking but American cheese is not. American cheese was discarded. Handouts with cheeses exempt from date marking were provided.

Refrigerated, ready to eat foods that require time and temperature control for safety (TCS) held at the establishment more than 24 hours shall be clearly dated and used or discarded w/in 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.

findings.title: Potentially hazardous foods properly thawed
findings.citation_text:
750.240 - Three pans of fish were observed on a cart and the counter in the kitchen upon arrival of the inspector. Surface temperatures were observed at 31°F and 38°F. Cook noted the fish was just removed from the walkin cooler prior to inspector's arrival. Pans of fish were placed back in the walkin cooler until additional kitchen help was able to begin proper thawing under running water prior to sevice. 

TCS foods shall be properly thawed by one of the  following methods: 1. Under refrigeration 41°F or below, 2. Under  potable running water 70°F/below with sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose food particles into the over-flow, 3. In microwave as part of the cooking process, or 4. As part of the cooking process.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.citation_text:
750.510 - Cook was observed washing hands without proper technique. Proper handwashing was discussed as was the use of only paper towels for wipe hands. 

Employees shall properly was hands any time they may have been contaminated, prior to putting on gloves/between glove changes, and prior to working with food, clean equipment, and unwrapped single service items.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.citation_text:
750.810 - Sanitizer solution was not setup in the kitchen for wiping surfaces. Maintain a bleach solution for wiping general surfaces during prep and food service. Store damp wiping cloths in solution between uses.
Also, use disposable paper towels and discard after use when spray bottles of bleach solution are used for wiping down surfaces.

Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
750.800b - The following food contact surfaces were soiled:
A) (R) metal baffle inside ice machine (mold buildup along lower edge);
B)  soda gun at banquet bar (black buildup in middle opening);   and
C) soda gun holder at the main bar (mold).

Clean and sanitize food contact surfaces between uses/as needed, up to every 4hrs after continuous use (for in-use items such as the can opener), to prevent cross contamination and eliminate buildup of debris.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
750.800e - The following non-food contact surfaces were soiled:
A) drip pan of stove (carbon/food debris); 
B) shelf above stove (grease);   and
C) buffet area in banquet room (food debris).

Clean non-food contact surfaces daily/as needed to eliminate buildup of debris.
NOTE: Food debris serves as a food for rodents. Clean the buffet line after every event.

findings.title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.citation_text:
750.880 - Storage bin for plastic utensils at the buffet area was soiled with food debris in the bottom. Clean out the storage bin as needed for utensils, and maintain it clean.

Single service items shall be stored, handled, and dispensed in a manner that protects items from potential contamination.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment:
750-1220 - Dead mouse and insects were observed on the glue trap behind the motor next to keg cooler at the banquet room bar. Change the glue trap.

All floors shall be maintained clean. Check on glue traps daily, and change them out as needed.

findings.title: Toxic items labeled and used properly
findings.citation_text:
750.1320 - Spray bottle labeled "bleach water solution" at the bar was at a concentration well above 200ppm chlorine. The test strip was bleached out when used to check the solution. Solution was diluted to 200ppm.

Chemicals must be used in accordance with directions on the label and must not be used in a manner that poses a risk of contamination to surfaces and/or potential harm to staff or patrons. Use test strips to verify concentration of bleach solution is maintained at 100-200ppm in spray bottles.

findings.title: Clean and soiled linen segregated and properly stored.
findings.comment:
750. 1380b - Damp and dry wiping cloths were observed in a storage rack at the bar. Bartender on duty stated they were probably left there from the previous evening. All wiping cloths were placed in the soiled linen storage area.

Soiled clothes and linens shall be stored in non-absorbent containers or washable laundry bags until removed for laundering. Properly store soiled linens.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.citation_text:
750.151 - A) Tomatoes for chili in the kitchen fridge had a date of 8/3. Tomatoes were removed to be discarded.
B) An open gallon of milk in the second kitchen fridge did not have a date mark and was less than 1/4 full. Milk was removed to be discarded.
C) Open container of cottage cheese was not dated in the second kitchen fridge. It appeared to be freshly opened recently (full to the top). Cottage cheese was dated and kept for use.
D) Green beans in the walkin cooler had a date of 8/22. The last day for use is today. Food service is not happening today. Green beans were to be discarded before the close of business today.

Refrigerated, potentially hazardous, ready to eat food held at the establishment more than 24 hours shall be clearly dated and used or discarded w/in 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.citation_text:
750.130 - A portion of raw ground beef was on the shelf of the fridge door next to a portion of cheese slices. Cheese slices were partially unwrapped and dried out, so cheese was discarded. Proper storage of raw and ready to eat foods was discussed.

All food shall be stored properly in order to prevent cross-contamination.  Store ready to eat foods above or away from raw foods.

findings.title: In-use food dispensing utensils properly stored.
findings.citation_text:
750.290 - Ice scoop was observed on a used aluminum foil lid on top of the ice machine. Store the ice scoop in a clean container. Make sure the scoop and the storage container are going through ware washing daily/as needed.

Ice scoop shall be stored on a clean surface or in the ice with the handle extended out of the ice.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
750.800e - The following non-food contact surfaces were soiled:
A) drip pan of flat grill (grease);  and
B) inside lower compartment of salad bar unit in banquet area (old mouse droppings).

Clean non-food contact surfaces daily/as needed to eliminate buildup of debris.

findings.title: Presence of insects/rodents.  Animals prohibited
findings.citation_text:
750.1160 - Laundry bag with soiled wiping cloths and towels in the kitchen had approximately a half dozen small flies in it. Soiled wiping cloths were placed in a sealed bag and moved to the chemical storage closet.
A few flies were also observed around the 3 part sink at the banquet room bar. Sinks need to be cleaned and use of fly strips in appropriate locations was discussed. A spot check will be conducted in the month of September to check on the status of pest control.

Effective measures to minimize the presence of rodents and insects shall be utilized. Provide effective pest control.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: See inspection report from 4/21/17 for details on original violations.

findings.comment: See inspection report from 4/21/17 for details on original violations.

findings.comment:

NEW: A gap was observed at the floor along the baseboard at the far left side under the pot/pan storage in the kitchen dry storage room. Repair the gap in the storage room.

findings.title: Foods handled with minimal manual contact
findings.citation_text:
750.160 & 280 - Employee was observed slicing onion and had bare hand contact with onion when it was rotated on the slicing apparatus. Use of gloves when handling and preparing ready to eat foods was discussed. Onions were done being sliced by the time the observation was made.
 
Ready to eat foods shall be handled in a manner to minimize direct hand contact. Use suitable utensils, such as gloves, tongs, scoops, etc., when handling ready to eat foods.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.citation_text:
750.510 & 512 - Employee doing dishes went between handling clean and dirty dishes without washing hands. Employee was advised on handwashing between tasks and was observed properly washing his hands prior to putting away any more clean dishes.

Cook was observed washing hands without proper technique. The manual faucet was shut off prior to retrieving paper towels to dry hands. Cook noted he was not getting ready to handle food but was then observed portioning pasta salad. Cook properly washed hands prior to continuing with food prep for lunch service. 

Employees (and volunteers) shall properly wash their hands any time hands may have been contaminated, upon entering the kitchen/before beginning any food handling/prep, before putting on gloves/between glove changes, and prior to working with food, clean equipment, and unwrapped single service articles. Always use proper technique when washing hands.
Educational handout on proper handwashing technique and when to wash hands were provided.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.citation_text:
750.690 - Sprayer head in dish area had heavy black mold buildup in the crevice of the sprayer surface. Employee noted he scrapes the buildup out of the sprayer head with a butter knife from time to time, but it does not get rid of the buildup. Thoroughly clean and sanitize the sprayer head. If it can not be properly cleaned and maintained as such, then replace it with one that can be maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

Pizza freezer at bar had heavy ice accumulation inside. Defrost the freezer.

Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
750.800b - The following food contact surfaces were soiled:
A) stem thermometer (stored in crevice of steam table);
B) can opener blade/crevice around blade (food debris/metal shavings) - taken to dish area to go through dish machine;   and
C) pizza oven tray at bar (food debris).

Clean and sanitize food contact surfaces between uses/as needed, up to every 4hrs after continuous use, to prevent cross contamination and eliminate buildup of debris.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.citation_text:
750.880 - Tray used for storage of plastic cups and other items was sticky along the front edges. Clean the tray as needed, and maintain it clean.

Plastic knives at the buffet in the banquet area were observed with handles and food contact surfaces intermixed and facing different directions. Place knives all facing one direction so persons retrieving knives will not touch/contaminate the food contact surfaces of knives that will be used by other customers.

Single service articles must be stored, handled, and dispensed in a manner that protects items form potential contamination.

findings.title: Plumbing installed and maintained
findings.citation_text:
750.1060 - Faucet at banquet room 3 part sink broke recently. Repair the 3 part sink.

All plumbing shall be sized, installed, and maintained in accordance with applicable provisions of the Illinois State Plumbing Code.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.citation_text:
750.1200 & 1220 - Old mouse droppings were observed in corners where areas of disrepair were noted at floor to wall junctures (holes in baseboard) in the kitchen dry storage room. Old droppings and debris were also observed under shelving and storage crates.

Old mouse droppings were observed on the floor in the following areas:
1. storage closets at the banquet area bar (vacuumed during inspection);
2. behind unused keg cooler at banquet area bar (vacuumed during inspection);   and
3. around the southwest corner and along the west side of the main bar.

Floor under popcorn machine cabinet at the bar was soiled with general debris. 

Floor under food storage shelves in walkin cooler was soiled.

 Thoroughly clean the floors throughout the facility, including under/behind equipment and in storage areas. Seal the holes in the corners of the baseboard in the dry storage room (potential hiding spots for pests - see general comments)

Floors must be in good repair, constructed to facilitate easy cleaning, and maintained clean. Junctures between walls and floors shall be coved and sealed.

findings.title: Toxic items labeled and used properly
findings.citation_text:
750.1320 - Spray bottle at bar labeled as bleach water contained so much bleach the inspector's test strip was bleached out, indicating the solution was too strong. Bartender stated she was pretty sure the maintenance worker mixes the solution prior to arrival of other staff. Solution in question is used to clean up spots on the floor but may also be used to wipe down the bar. Solution was diluted during the inspection to be at ~200ppm chlorine.

Chemicals must be used in accordance with directions on the label and must not be used in a manner that poses a risk of contamination to surfaces and/or potential harm to staff or patrons. Use test strips to verify concentration of bleach solution is maintained at 100-200ppm in spray bottles.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment: 750-151(a)  Observed slices of turkey meat in the upright kitchen fridge #2 to not be date marked. There were a number of gallons of milk around the facility without proper date marking too. And, observed an unlabeled container of corn on the bottom shelf of the walk-in cooler (item from 12/16).  Also, there was a container of cheese sauce marked 12/8/16 on the bottom shelf of the walk-in cooler. Discarded during the inspection.  Refrigerated potentially hazardous ready to eat food held at the establishment more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked with the date or day by which the food shall be consumed, sold, or discarded. Maximum holding time at 41°F is 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment: 750-690 Observed cardboard on the bottom shelf of one of the upright freezers in the banquet room. Cease use of cardboard. Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

findings.title: Sanitizing concentration
findings.comment: 750-830 Observed the dish machine to not be properly sanitizing. The facility has a three compartment sink able to be used for sanitizing. Kitchen was closed during the inspection. Facility is going to GFS for additional sanitizing product. All chemical sanitizers in a dish machine must meet the requirements of 21 CFR 178.1010 to ensure all items are properly sanitized.  Rinse water shall not less than 75F. Provide proper sanitizer concentration.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: 750-800e Observed the bottom of the first upright cooler in the kitchen to have blood drips within the bottom drawers. Clean the drawers.  Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.comment: 750-880 Observed a bulk box of single-service cups on the floor of the dry storage room. Store single-service at least 6" off the floor. Single-service articles shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in closed cartons or containers which protect them from contamination and shall not be placed under exposed sewer lines or  water lines, except for automatic fire protection sprinkler heads may be required by law.

findings.title: Plumbing installed and maintained
findings.comment: 750-1060 Observed the middle sink of the banquet bar triple sink to be plugged. Sink was eeled during the inspection. The drain is moving, however, slow. See that this drain is properly eeled. All plumbing shall be sized, installed, and maintained in accordance with applicable provisions of the Illinois State Plumbing Code.
